summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with HLA-B27-positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and depression, was admitted for acute worsening of mid-back and bilateral SI joint pain that began suddenly the night prior. He reported a fever of 102°F several days before admission but was afebrile during hospitalization. Labs showed mildly elevated inflammatory markers without leukocytosis. An X-ray of the cervical and thoracic spine showed mild degenerative changes but no fracture or ankylosis. Pain was managed with increased hydromorphone and addition of tizanidine for muscle spasms. The patient declined earlier rheumatology follow-up and MRI/CT evaluation. He improved symptomatically and was discharged home with instructions to monitor for worsening pain, fever, or neurological symptoms, and to follow up with his primary care provider.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
